Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (BOE-A-2010-6737), as developed by Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010) and as subsequently amended; Real Decreto 188/2021, de 9 de marzo, por el que se regula la obligación de información sobre titulares reales (central UBO register); and Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (EU AML Regulation) applicable from 2027.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A virtual office is accepted for the statutory registered address (domicilio social) of the SL at incorporation stage, provided a real administrative mailbox and accessible seat exist. However, for ISIC 5621 airline inflight catering, a purely virtual arrangement is not permissible for the licensed activity: the operator must maintain a physically licensed production kitchen, bonded storage facilities, and ramp-delivery logistics base at or near the airport. The registered office and the operational premises may legally differ, but both must be genuine, verifiable, and subject to inspection by the relevant authorities.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Competent corporate registry

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 21-34 (Incorporation), 58-62 (Share Capital), 62-63 (Registered Office), 209-213 (Administrators); Royal Decree-Law 13/2010 on incorporation by standard bylaws.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed for inscription in the Registro Mercantil.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 59 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Minimum share capital for an SL is EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,570), fully subscribed and fully paid in at incorporation; contributions in cash must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution and may be released only after registry inscription, as provided in Article 62 LSC.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certificate from local firefighters (certificado de protección contra incendios) after inspection; structural load inspection certificate for the production area, blast chilling units, and delivery loading bays; occupational workplace clearance under the Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, including the non-hazardous labor conditions report and employee training certificates.

Paid-in capital rule: Minimum share capital for an SL is EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,570), fully subscribed and fully paid in at incorporation; contributions in cash must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution and may be released only after registry inscription, as provided in Article 62 LSC.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)

E-government filing portal

A foreign promoter must first request a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) for the proposed Spanish SL from AEAT before the public deed is executed before a notary. After incorporation of the SL and registration with the Commercial Registry, the definitive NIF is obtained by filing Form 030. The SL must also file Form 036/037 to register in the Census of Entrepreneurs, notify the commencement of activity (including the relevant IAE economic activity epigraph), and complete VAT registration. For a branch of a foreign entity operating in Spain, the branch obtains its own NIF through Form 036/037, and the foreign head office must evidence fulfilment of Spanish registration thresholds if applicable.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — A foreign promoter must first request a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) for the proposed Spanish SL from AEAT before the public deed is executed before a notary. After incorporation of the SL and registration with the Commercial Registry, the definitive NIF is obtained by filing Form 030. The SL must also file Form 036/037 to register in the Census of Entrepreneurs, notify the commencement of activity (including the relevant IAE economic activity epigraph), and complete VAT registration. For a branch of a foreign entity operating in Spain, the branch obtains its own NIF through Form 036/037, and the foreign head office must evidence fulfilment of Spanish registration thresholds if applicable.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

Spain does not have a check-the-box or multicurrency entity classification regime. The Spanish SL is per se a resident corporation subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades at 25% (reduced rates apply to newly created SMEs and other specific cases). The principal statutory elections available are: (i) the election to form and be taxed as a consolidated corporate tax group under articles 58-70 of the LIS; (ii) the VAT group election (régimen de Grupo de Entidades) available under Spanish VAT law and Royal Decree-Law 8/2023; and (iii) the entitlement to the 95% participation exemption on dividends and capital gains, which is claimed in the corporate income tax return upon satisfaction of substantive conditions. Hybrid mismatch elections are not permitted; the ATAD hybrid mismatch rules are directly applicable as overriding anti-abuse measures.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No minimum turnover threshold applies to a Spanish tax resident SL; VAT registration in the Census of Entrepreneurs is mandatory before commencement of business activities by filing Form 036/037. For non-established taxable persons, any taxable supply in Spain may trigger registration; for intra-Community distance sales subject to the Union scheme, the cross-border threshold is EUR 10,000.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Zero-rating for export is available under article 21 of the Spanish VAT Act for goods physically leaving the EU customs territory. The exporting entity must hold ownership of the goods, ensure dispatch to a destination outside the EU (including Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla), and obtain a customs export declaration accepted by the Spanish customs office. For airline in-flight catering, the supply of meals and provisions to aircraft operating international routes may qualify either as an export when goods are loaded onto aircraft departing to non-EU destinations or as a supply for the provisioning of aircraft under the VAT exemption for international aviation, provided the airline operates international services and the documentary evidence of boarding and destination flight is maintained. Goods must physically leave the EU within 90 days of dispatch, and supporting proof of exit must be produced within three months; otherwise the zero-rating is denied and VAT becomes due.

  • Customs Export Declaration (D.U.A. / Single Administrative Document or equivalent electronic export declaration)
  • Air Waybill, Bill of Lading or CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure from the EU
  • Export invoice and packed list describing the in-flight meal products
  • Payment evidence such as SWIFT MT103, bank certificate or airline settlement receipt proving remittance of proceeds
  • Carrier certificate confirming the date of departure and the destination airport as a non-EU/third-country destination

Spain requires electronic invoicing and digital reporting through Veri*Factu under Royal Decree 1007/2023. Private-sector invoices must be produced using certified invoicing software that generates a standard XML representation with a QR code and maintains a chronological record of issuance, modification, cancellation and transmission for AEAT. The system operates as near-real-time digital deposit rather than pre-clearance; there is no tax authority stamping before invoice delivery. Invoices to Spanish public administrations must be e-invoiced in FacturaE XML through the FACe portal.

AEAT will reverse any zero-rated export if the mandatory export documentation is not retained within the specified deadlines or if the physical exit is not corroborated by customs records. Where zero-rating is rejected, the taxable supply is retroactively assessed at 21% VAT plus late payment interest. False or fabricated export declarations constitute tax fraud: administrative penalties range from 50% to 100% of the unpaid VAT, may include total loss of exemption and refund claims, and criminal liability arises where the defrauded VAT exceeds EUR 120,000 in a single tax year, with potential imprisonment for responsible directors or legal representatives.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a full Eurozone member and maintains full liberalization of both current and capital account transactions under Articles 63-65 TFEU. The euro is freely convertible with no exchange control license, prior-authorization, or approval requirement for business transactions. Profit and dividend remittance abroad is unrestricted: after corporate income tax settlement, non-resident shareholders are subject to domestic 19% withholding (Article 21 Non-Resident Income Tax Act), treaty-reduced to 5-15% under Spain-LATAM tax treaties, with the remittance executed without central bank permission upon presentation of Form 216 to the Tax Agency and proof of the treasury's tax filing. The only practical hurdles are documentary conduct under Spanish AML rules and the mandatory statistical declaration of foreign transactions; convertibility risk is zero for EUR and material only for customers operating in Latin American non-fully-convertible currencies, which are not a statutory barrier for the catering activity.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Statutory surrender ratio: 0% - Spain imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or retention obligation for export proceeds. Receive-and-retain freedom applies to aviation catering receipts, aircraft provisioning settlements, and other invoiced exports from the Spanish SL to non-resident airlines. Reporting duty: all transactions with non-residents exceeding EUR 10,000 per operation (or EUR 50,000 per calendar year per client) must be declared to the Banco de España through the Declaración de Operaciones con el Exterior (OGD) platform; invoice and SWIFT records must be retained for six years. No repatriation timeline applies, and no Banco de España approval is required for keeping or spending foreign-currency balances.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) acting as the national central bank and supervisory authority for financial institutions; foreign exchange administration and the statistical foreign-investment registry are jointly executed by the Directorate General for International Transactions of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores) and by SEPBLAC (Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Infringements) under Law 10/2010.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Wise Fit: High

MEDIUM as a primary operating account; HIGH as an auxiliary disbursement/collections rail. EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions passporting into Spain under PSD2 (e.g., Wise Business, Revolut Business, Qonto, Penta) permit remote onboarding, SEPA Credit Transfers, SCT Inst, and SWIFT payments; however, they may not take deposits or issue credit, cannot issue the banker's deposit certificate needed to evidence the capital injection in the Mercantile Registry, and airlines/Aena settlement systems will generally require a Spanish credit-institution IBAN. Legal constraints: EMIs fall within Law 10/2010 SEPBLAC supervision, must safeguard client funds in segregated accounts, and treasury products (FX forwards/options) are not offered on balance sheet; therefore the capital escrow and primary settlement account must reside at a Banco de España-supervised bank.

Revolut Fit: High

MEDIUM as a primary operating account; HIGH as an auxiliary disbursement/collections rail. EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions passporting into Spain under PSD2 (e.g., Wise Business, Revolut Business, Qonto, Penta) permit remote onboarding, SEPA Credit Transfers, SCT Inst, and SWIFT payments; however, they may not take deposits or issue credit, cannot issue the banker's deposit certificate needed to evidence the capital injection in the Mercantile Registry, and airlines/Aena settlement systems will generally require a Spanish credit-institution IBAN. Legal constraints: EMIs fall within Law 10/2010 SEPBLAC supervision, must safeguard client funds in segregated accounts, and treasury products (FX forwards/options) are not offered on balance sheet; therefore the capital escrow and primary settlement account must reside at a Banco de España-supervised bank.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident UBO or director lacking Spanish NIE, with tax residence in a Latin American or third-country jurisdiction, triggering enhanced due diligence.

Root cause: Non-resident UBO or director lacking Spanish NIE, with tax residence in a Latin American or third-country jurisdiction, triggering enhanced due diligence.

Defense evidence: Valid passports; NIE certificates; full UBO ownership chain; tax residence certificate (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) of the UBO; apostilled corporate registry excerpt; 24-month source-of-wealth file (tax returns, salary and asset sale records); bank reference letter from the UBO's primary bank; written purpose statement describing the inflight catering investment and projected annual flows.
Capital injection wired from a third-party account, from an FATF-grey-list jurisdiction, or from a jurisdiction with currency controls.

Root cause: Capital injection wired from a third-party account, from an FATF-grey-list jurisdiction, or from a jurisdiction with currency controls.

Defense evidence: Escritura de ampliación de capital; shareholder resolution authorizing the transfer; MT103/SWIFT execution notice proving the originator is the registered shareholder; six months of originator bank statements; underlying aviation catering contracts; audited financials of the shareholder if a holding company; any third-party remittance must be rejected and re-wired only from the shareholder's own account.
Transaction profile mismatched with ISIC 5621 declared activity or absence of statutory food safety/airport licenses.

Root cause: Transaction profile mismatched with ISIC 5621 declared activity or absence of statutory food safety/airport licenses.

Defense evidence: Autorización sanitaria issued under Regulation (EC) 852/2004 and Royal Decree 191/2011; Aena airport access and ramp handling authorization or concession sub-permit; signed airline catering agreements or LOIs; monthly billing projections; payroll plan demonstrating operational staff; treasury questionnaire aligned to Aviation_Contract_Wire and monthly ACH/SEPA rails.
Low registered share capital of the SL relative to forecast CapEx of the catering kitchen, creating a shell/brass-plate suspicion.

Root cause: Low registered share capital of the SL relative to forecast CapEx of the catering kitchen, creating a shell/brass-plate suspicion.

Defense evidence: Notarial deed and bank certificate evidencing actual funded capital in the escrow account; CapEx budget for kitchen equipment, vehicles, and ramp assets; leasing/tenancy agreements for the airport facility; employer liability and aviation product liability insurance; employment contract register for kitchen and logistics staff.
PEP status or adverse media screening of the UBO or administrador.

Root cause: PEP status or adverse media screening of the UBO or administrador.

Defense evidence: Detailed PEP declaration listing positions, institutions, and end dates; employment/career certificate; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds report; criminal record certificates; signatory authority matrix; commitment letter accepting quarterly compliance reviews; proactive escalation to the bank's Compliance Committee with the full dossier.
Parallel use of a fintech EMI account for aviation receivables, raising concerns about transaction-flow concealment.

Root cause: Parallel use of a fintech EMI account for aviation receivables, raising concerns about transaction-flow concealment.

Defense evidence: Treasury policy letter naming the Tier-1 bank as the single settlement institution and defining the EMI as a pass-through collections rail; EMI bank statements shown to be pass-through only; approved FX hedging policy; quarterly reconciliation of EMI and Tier-1 account statements delivered to the compliance officer.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant injection protocol: (1) execute the escritura de constitución or ampliación de capital before a Spanish notary; (2) obtain the definitive NIF and NIE for signatories; (3) open a designated capital escrow account at a Tier-1 Spanish bank; (4) file or cause the bank to file the statistical foreign-investment declaration through the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores of the Ministry of Economy (for investments exceeding EUR 3,005,006.06 the declaration is due within 30 days post-injection; lower amounts are captured in the bank's periodic balance-of-payments declaration); (5) instruct the inbound SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own account using field 50K with the exact corporate remitter, field 59 with the SL's IBAN, and field 70 containing APORTACION CAPITAL SOCIAL / AMPLIACION DE CAPITAL - [SL name], Escritura [notary/protocol reference]; (6) deliver the deed, shareholder resolution, and source-of-funds dossier to compliance; (7) after credit, obtain the certificado bancario de depósito and complete the Mercantile Registry registration. A préstamo participativo (participating loan) may substitute for equity, but the wire narrative must state PRESTAMO PARTICIPATIVO and the loan agreement must be notarized to be accepted by the bank.EU supplier payments settle via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA B2B Direct Debit (mapped to the Monthly_ACH rail); non-EU supplier disbursements (raw proteins, packaging materials, Latin American imports) are cleared by SWIFT MT103 with full correspondent instructions (field 56A/57A), and for documentary trade, Commercial Letters of Credit are issued by SWIFT MT700 (UCP 600) with claims drawn by MT103/MT754 against transport and sanitary certificates. Airline contract receivables are collected on the Aviation_Contract_Wire rail either through the IATA CASS aviation settlement cycle or by monthly bank wire per the catering agreement, denominated in EUR or USD; any USD wire is cleared through the Spanish bank's New York correspondent using Fedwire/CHIPS. Each non-EUR payment above EUR 50,000 per year is captured in the OGD balance-of-payments filing.OTC Outright FX Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) executed with Banco de España-supervised credit institutions; no clearing obligation for non-financial counterparties below EMIR thresholds.FX Swaps (spot/forward combinations) for short-term EUR/USD treasury conversion and month-end liquidity management.Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR/USD CCS) under an ISDA Master Agreement with mandatory EMIR trade reporting to an ESMA-registered trade repository.Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for restricted Latin American currencies (ARS, COP, CLP) where local convertibility limits apply; permissible only as hedging and subject to EMIR reporting.Vanilla FX Options (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) purchased OTC from an EU-authorized investment firm; each execution requires completion of MiFID II appropriateness testing and a written hedge-only, no-speculation treasury policy.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: MEDIUM as a primary operating account; HIGH as an auxiliary disbursement/collections rail. EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions passporting into Spain under PSD2 (e.g., Wise Business, Revolut Business, Qonto, Penta) permit remote onboarding, SEPA Credit Transfers, SCT Inst, and SWIFT payments; however, they may not take deposits or issue credit, cannot issue the banker's deposit certificate needed to evidence the capital injection in the Mercantile Registry, and airlines/Aena settlement systems will generally require a Spanish credit-institution IBAN. Legal constraints: EMIs fall within Law 10/2010 SEPBLAC supervision, must safeguard client funds in segregated accounts, and treasury products (FX forwards/options) are not offered on balance sheet; therefore the capital escrow and primary settlement account must reside at a Banco de España-supervised bank.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% (general corporate income tax rate under Article 29 of Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law 27/2014; 15% preferential rate for newly created SLs carrying on an economic activity in the first two eligible tax periods).

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% statutory Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) on dividends distributed by a Spanish SL to a non-resident beneficial owner (Art. 25.4 TRLIRNR). The rate is reduced to 0% for qualifying EU/EEA parent companies under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU, and to 5%, 10% or 15% under applicable double-tax treaties, depending on ownership and the particular treaty.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

The return must be filed within 25 calendar days after the lapse of six months from the end of the tax period. For a SL with a fiscal year ending 31 December, the deadline is 30 November of the following year.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 / Cabecera - Identificación del contribuyente Complete legal name, NIF, registered address, main CNAE activity code (5621 for airport catering), and tax administration territorial code of the filing Spanish tax office. Enter the Spanish NIF of the SL only. If non-resident shareholders or directors are involved, do not enter their foreign ID in the main header unless required in the annex schedule; list foreign controlling entity data in the 'participaciones significativas' section. Late filing without prior official request triggers a graduated surcharge under Art. 27 LGT: 5% within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. If the AEAT issues a formal assessment for non-filing, the surcharge is replaced by a tax infringement sanction under Arts. 191–193 LGT, ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount. In addition, the SL may be barred from eligibility for EU funds and state aids, and administrators may incur subsistence responsibility for unpaid tax debts.
Box 2 / Período impositivo Set the start and end dates of the tax period (DD/MM/YYYY). For a newly incorporated SL, the period opens on the incorporation date and closes on 31 December or the date approved in by-laws, without exceeding 12 months. Use the statutory accounting period of the Spanish SL. A different period can be used only if expressly approved by the AEAT; non-resident parent accounting periods are not relevant unless a PE is maintained in Spain. Late filing without prior official request triggers a graduated surcharge under Art. 27 LGT: 5% within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. If the AEAT issues a formal assessment for non-filing, the surcharge is replaced by a tax infringement sanction under Arts. 191–193 LGT, ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount. In addition, the SL may be barred from eligibility for EU funds and state aids, and administrators may incur subsistence responsibility for unpaid tax debts.
Box 3 / Resultado contable y ajustes extracontables Report the accounting profit or loss from financial statements and reconcile it to taxable income with permanent and temporary adjustments under Art. 10 and 11 LIS (non-deductible expenses, amortisation, provisions, exempt income). If the SL has a non-resident shareholder, ensure that dividends from foreign subsidiaries are properly segregated if the participation exemption under Art. 21 LIS is claimed. Interest or royalty payments to a non-resident owner may be subject to non-deductibility rules if the debt exceeds safe harbours (thin capitalisation). Late filing without prior official request triggers a graduated surcharge under Art. 27 LGT: 5% within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. If the AEAT issues a formal assessment for non-filing, the surcharge is replaced by a tax infringement sanction under Arts. 191–193 LGT, ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount. In addition, the SL may be barred from eligibility for EU funds and state aids, and administrators may incur subsistence responsibility for unpaid tax debts.
Box 4 / Compensación de bases imponibles negativas (BIN) Offset tax-loss carryforwards from prior years against positive taxable income, respecting the annual offset limits (70% or 50% of the positive base). Only losses generated by the Spanish SL may be offset. Losses from foreign PEs or from participation in non-res ident entities are not freely offset unless they have been recognized through the Spanish permanent establishment regime. Non-resident shareholders may not personally use the SL's BIN. Late filing without prior official request triggers a graduated surcharge under Art. 27 LGT: 5% within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. If the AEAT issues a formal assessment for non-filing, the surcharge is replaced by a tax infringement sanction under Arts. 191–193 LGT, ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount. In addition, the SL may be barred from eligibility for EU funds and state aids, and administrators may incur subsistence responsibility for unpaid tax debts.
Box 5 / Cuota íntegra y deducciones Apply the applicable tax rate (25% or 15% for new companies) to the taxable base, then apply tax credits, bonuses and deductions (double taxation, R&D, reinvestment of profits). Report credit for foreign tax paid on income sourced abroad if the SL is the taxpayer and a DTA is relevant. For non-residents, do not apply Spanish tax credits to their own foreign income; the SL's tax credits are computed separately. Late filing without prior official request triggers a graduated surcharge under Art. 27 LGT: 5% within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. If the AEAT issues a formal assessment for non-filing, the surcharge is replaced by a tax infringement sanction under Arts. 191–193 LGT, ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount. In addition, the SL may be barred from eligibility for EU funds and state aids, and administrators may incur subsistence responsibility for unpaid tax debts.
Box 6 / Cuota líquida, retenciones e ingresos a cuenta Calculate the final tax payable or refund receivable after deducting withholdings made during the year (including payments on account made by the SL on its own income) and inputting the amount of corporate tax already prepaid. The SL must declare and remit withholding tax on outbound payments to non-resident suppliers (Form 123) and file Form 286/210 where applicable. Non-resident beneficial owners do not have access to the SL's 'cuota líquida' reduction except through dividend distribution or transfer of shares. Late filing without prior official request triggers a graduated surcharge under Art. 27 LGT: 5% within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. If the AEAT issues a formal assessment for non-filing, the surcharge is replaced by a tax infringement sanction under Arts. 191–193 LGT, ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount. In addition, the SL may be barred from eligibility for EU funds and state aids, and administrators may incur subsistence responsibility for unpaid tax debts.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 10,000,000 net turnover in the preceding tax period triggers mandatory preparation of both the Master File and the Local File. A Local File is also required when the aggregate value of related-party transactions exceeds EUR 250,000 per category of goods/services, even if the turnover is below EUR 10,000,000. Transactions under these thresholds remain subject to the arm's-length rule but may benefit from simplified documentation relief.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not have a formal 'Economic Substance Regulations' regime like certain offshore jurisdictions, but it enforces substance over form through the general anti-abuse doctrine (Art. 15 LGT), the principle of reality in commercial transactions, and the ATAD-compliant CFC rules. A catering SL must demonstrate actual management, employee payroll, kitchen and ramp equipment, storage, invoicing, and decision-taking in Spain. Without this substance, the AEAT may disregard the entity for corporate income tax and treaty purposes, recharacterise interposed operations, and impose fraud penalties. For the airline catering business, no onshore tax regime incentive is conditioned on substance beyond ordinary Spain residence, but the functional profile must support the transfer-pricing analysis.
